w: On 27 May 1970, in London, David Blundy, a reporter from the weekly "Sunday Times", came to meet Yogiji Maharaj. He held a spiritual question and answer session with Swamishri. Some extracts from it:
David: "What will your activities be in England?"
Swamishri: "Those of satsang, nothing else..."
David: "Do the mental worries, physical ailments and troubles of those who come here for darshan go away or not?"

Swamishri: "They go away. By the darshan of God and the Sant, mental worries, physical ailments and troubles go away. That is certain, but darshan should be done with an understanding of their glory."
David: "Have you ever had any worries, ailments or troubles?"
Swamishri: "Never in my life..."
David: "Do you enjoy England?"
Swamishri: "We liked England. We found peace. Our ishtadev (chosen deity), Shriji Maharaj, came here in a divine form to take Sir Malcolm to His abode, so we liked England."
"Shriji Maharaj came here in a divine form, so we liked it." In this way Swamishri gave the reason as the connection with Shriji Maharaj, not the comfort and prosperity here.

2003.o: 111th Yogi Jayanti Festival and Completion of 700 Sadhus
w: In the morning Swamishri visited Yogi Smruti Mandir for darshan and blessed the sadhus by instructing all on how to scale the heights of saintliness that Yogiji Maharaj lived and preached.
Swamishri fulfilled the desire of Yogiji Maharaj to initiate 700 sadhus. Swamishri gave sadhu and parshad dikshas to 31 youths and blessed the assembly. (See special report)
In the evening, the 111th birthday of Yogiji Maharaj was celebrated on the mandir grounds. (See special report)
A devotee came for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Today, on the occasion of his fiftieth wedding anniversary, he offered all his savings at the feet of Thakorji.
Swamishri asked, "How many years have you been married?"
"Fifty years."

Addressing the youths standing around, Swamishri said, "Listen, it is fifty years since he was married, and there has never been any unhappiness." Saying this, he asked the devotee, "Was there ever any quarrel?"
With a little hesitation and shyness he said, "Well, that is bound to happen!"
"Then what did you do at that time?"
"Bore it, compromised," the devotee said.

This was exactly the answer Swamishri expected. So, addressing the youths, he said, "That's it, just keep this much in mind. In family life there will be happiness and sorrow, at home there will be words with each other, but bear with each other. Compromise a little, and there will be happiness. Here, a year passes and they celebrate a wedding anniversary, but there is no telling how long it will last. No one has any tolerance!"
Again he asked the devotee, "Did you ever celebrate your marriage (your wedding anniversaries)?"
"No."

Swamishri said, "Here they spend so much money on wedding anniversaries." Then, looking at the youths, he said, "We should not celebrate weddings and such, and not hold parties. We should offer devotion. If you really want to, sponsor a meal for Thakorji."
Swamishri naturally taught the young generation how to stay well in family life.

On 27 May 2004, in Edison, Pramukh Swami Maharaj finished the assembly at 8.20 pm and came down from the stage to return to his residence. Then, referring to Swamishri's packed programmes, Prafullbhai Raja, the managing volunteer of the Edison mandir, said, "Bapa! Please forgive us. You have to endure a lot of hardship."
Swamishri said, "If God's seva gets done and God's worship gets done, such hardship is good. Yogiji Maharaj used to say that hardship is devotion. So one is meant to remain in that hardship."
Prafullbhai said, "I am saying this for your sake. We are going to endure hardship anyway."
Swamishri said, "If you have hardship, then we must have it too, mustn't we!"

It is a fact that despite his old age Swamishri exerts himself greatly and endures great hardship, but whenever devotees speak of hardship, one gets a special darshan of Swamishri's enthusiasm for enduring it.
(27 May 2004, Edison)

On the night of 27 May 2004, when Pramukh Swami Maharaj, having finished his meetings, came to his rest room, he was going towards the sofa to sit. So the attendant sadhu said, "Every day you go to rest late. So it would be good if today you went to rest ten minutes early."

Pointing to Dharmacharan Swami, who looks after the seva of letter writing, Swamishri said, "He goes around carrying this portfolio. So let us finish the letters too in ten minutes." Saying this, Swamishri sat on the sofa. He read letters for fifteen minutes and then went to rest.
Swamishri has never held back in making good use of every single moment. The tendency to put off work never even crosses his mind.
(27 May 2004, Edison)

The city corporation or council members honoured Swamishri in the evening satsang assembly at the mandir. Prior to this Viveksagar Swami discoursed on the Vachanamrut and BAPS tribal children performed a tribal dance. Thereafter, Shri Kanjibhai MP had a painting on Mahatma Gandhi receiving the blessings of Shastriji Maharaj during his Dandi March unveiled at the hands of Swamishri. Gandhiji had met Shastriji Maharaj in the village of Navagam on 13 March 1930. The painting depicting the historic incident would be displayed in the exhibition on Gandhiji at Dandi. Shri Nitinbhai Kansara, Executive Chairman of Navsari Municipality, read the citation before presenting it to Swamishri. Then the office bearers of various leading organizations of Navsari also presented separate citations to honour Swamishri: Vijalpur Corporation, Navsari District Office, Chamber of Commerce, representative of Kabilpor village office, Rotary Club, Manav Kalyan Trust, Saiyaji Vaibhav Library, Health Centre and Yogasan Organization, Agrawal Community, BJP Youth Wing, President of Navsari District, BJP President of Ahwa-Dang district, Kutch Kadva Patidar Samaj, Prajapati Samaj and Giants Club. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly expressing that the honour and accolades offered were all due to the efforts and grace of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj.

At 10.00 am Swamishri departed by flight from Dar-es-Salaam and landed at Moi International Airport in Mombasa at 10.30 am. After having darshan of Thakorji at the BAPS hari mandir Swamishri and sadhus were welcomed at a devoteee’s bungalow in Nyali by the ocean shore. Swamishri inaugurated his four storey bungalow.

Today was the official 60th Pramukh Varni Din – the day Shastriji Maharaj appointed Swamishri as the president of the BAPS. Bhajans about the glory of Swamishri were sung by sadhus during his puja. Thereafter, senior sadhus honoured Swamishri with garlands and shawls. Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti of murtis for BAPS hari mandirs in Barshi, Dahanu, Jamge, Nanded and Kankrali.
Addiction is poison

6 May 2009, Mumbai A youth who had an addiction came to Swamishri. He ate ghutka (shredded tobacco with flavour). Swamishri questioned, “Do you feel that your addiction is wrong?” “Yes.” “Then give it up. How long does it take to quit for someone who thinks it is wrong!” “I’ll give it up slowly,” the youth replied mildly. “Will you take poison if I give it to you?” Swamishri asked explicitly. “No.” “Tobacco is poison. You shouldn’t give it up slowly. If someone were to tell you to go to America after all the arrangements were made, would you go slowly? Similarly, you should quit in one go. Pray to God and you’ll be able to give it up.” Swamishri blessed the youth.
For the sake of one’s child

15 May 2009, Mumbai A father and son came for Swamishri’s darshan and blessings. The son was of a tender age. His father was habituated to drinking alcohol. Swamishri asked him, “How would you feel if your son started drinking?” The father remained silent. Swamishri asked the child, “What does your father drink?” Before the boy could answer his father averred, “He doesn’t know as yet?” Swamishri picked up his words and advised, “When he comes to know and starts drinking, how will you react?” Give it up for the sake of your child. There is no need to drink liquor at all. Everything other than eating, praying to God and looking after one’s responsibilities is wasteful.”Swamishri’s words produced a desirable effect.

Swamishri presided over the Yagna for World Peace and performed the pujan of murtis to be consecrated in the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir. Swamishri also performed the pratishtha rituals of the BAPS hari mandir in Chachana. In the evening a grand, colourful 2 km long procession was carried out on the streets of Limbdi. For details see pp. 4-11.

ds.t: A continuous dhun against the wind
w: Since yesterday, Pramukh Swami Maharaj had started a continuous dhun so that the problem of the wind would be resolved and the wind would stay under control, and he had given instructions about it two or three times. Today too, when Narayanmuni Swami came to meet Swamishri, he said to Swamishri, "The dhun is going on, but there is a procession this evening, so what should we do? Shall we stop the dhun at that time?"
Swamishri said, "No, let five people stay. Keep the dhun going."
"Shall we stop it in the evening at the time of the sandhya arti?"
"Start it again tomorrow after the mangla arti, and keep the dhun going until the installation festival is celebrated tomorrow."

And the dhun yagna continued without a break. The problem of the wind resolved itself in time. The installation festival was celebrated supremely, without any obstacle. Everyone realised that the yagna of Swamishri's faith always bears fruit.

Since yesterday, Pramukh Swami Maharaj had begun a continuous dhun so that the problem of the wind would be resolved and kept in check, and he had given instructions about it two or three times. Today too, when Narayanmuni Swami came to meet Swamishri, he told Swamishri, "The dhun is going on, but there is a procession in the evening, so what should we do? Shall we stop the dhun at that time?"
Swamishri said, "No, let five people stay. Keep the dhun going."
"Shall we stop it at the evening arti?"
"Start it again tomorrow after the mangla arti, and keep the dhun going until the installation festival is celebrated tomorrow."

And the dhun yagna went on continuously. The problem of the wind resolved itself in time. The installation festival was celebrated supremely without any obstacle. Everyone realised that Swamishri's yagna of faith always bears fruit.

Tonight, after the meal was over, the parshads presented a debate titled "The Last Birth," in which half the parshads argued that "this is our last birth," while the other half were forcefully putting forward the understanding, "No, the last birth will come after taking 2, 4 or 5 births." No decision was being reached. So the final decision was left to the supreme court, Mahant Swami Maharaj. Three options were placed before Swamishri.
1. "This is the last birth: reality"
2. "This is the last birth: consolation" and
3. "Other"
Swamishri raised the board "This is the last birth: reality." Then he himself asked for the microphone and said:

"Naradji went to find a bridegroom for King Ambarish's daughter. When he came back, 10 generations of the girl's family had passed. So even if 10 births happen, it is nothing to reckon with. Swami said in his talks, 'However he may be, he will take him to Akshardham within five births.' Compared with countless births, five births are nothing, so it is the last birth."

Looking at it another way: "Wherever those five births are to be taken, there will be contact with the great sadhu. And where there is contact with the great sadhu, it is Akshardham itself. So however many births there may be, there will be contact with the great sadhu, so it is the last birth. 99% of the work is done. But there is still that 1%!"
